title: Remove dead ConventionsConfig plumbing left over from the deviation-engine swap
description:
sutra/234 (bc7704e) replaced convention violations with an on-the-fly deviation report, but left the FCA-era config surface in place. It parses and does nothing:

- `Rules.conventions: ConventionsConfig` (src/rules.rs:446, struct at :523) — `suppress` + `exempt`, both still deserialized from `.sutra/rules.toml`
- `ConventionExemption` (src/rules.rs:531)
- `FcaEngine::check` (src/conventions/engine.rs:222) — the only reader of `config.suppress`/`config.exempt`; every caller is inside its own `mod tests`
- `ConventionViolation` and its re-export in src/conventions/mod.rs, if nothing else uses them

The live path is `conventions::detect_deviations` (src/conventions/engine.rs:432), called from src/tools/review.rs:459. It takes no ConventionsConfig.

Why this matters beyond dead code: `sutra_conventions` still mines and lists conventions (2048 in the arjuna workspace), so a suppress list looks live. During arjuna/3 an agent spent real effort semantically re-resolving 54 suppress hashes across a workspace re-root before discovering nothing consumes them.

Known affected file: sutra's own .sutra/rules.toml:373 carries a 9-entry suppress block. It is the only rules.toml under ~/soft and ~/nhs that still has one (arjuna's was removed in arjuna@5ad3f5b).

Note on scope: this is removal of the orphaned FCA config only. Whether the deviation engine should grow its own suppression surface is deliberately NOT part of this task — Josh is waiting on real-world deviation-report output before deciding. Don't design a replacement here.

Sequencing: since Josh may still want a suppression surface later, consider whether to delete the `[conventions]` parse outright or keep it as a deprecation shim for one cycle. Leaning delete — but see the acceptance criterion about silence.

acceptance_criteria.text: ConventionsConfig, ConventionExemption, FcaEngine::check and their tests are gone, along with any now-unused ConventionViolation plumbing

A [conventions] block in a rules.toml no longer parses silently into a no-op. Rules has no deny_unknown_fields, so simply deleting the field swaps one silence for another — emit a ConstraintParseError (or equivalent surfaced warning) naming the block as removed, so existing workspaces are told rather than ignored
sutra's own .sutra/rules.toml:373 suppress block is removed in the same change
cargo test passes; sutra_review on the sutra workspace still returns deviations

execution_record:
Went as planned. Removed ConventionsConfig, ConventionExemption, FcaEngine::check + its 10 tests + setup helper, and ConventionViolation (struct + mod.rs re-export). check_inverse/ConventionMatch left intact — out of scope and not FCA-config readers.

For the deny_unknown_fields gap: kept the Rules.conventions field as a private Option<toml::Value> catch-all; when Some, all_constraints pushes a ConstraintParseError(name="conventions") telling the user the block is removed. Rewrote the three old parse_* tests to assert this deprecation behavior instead of the old suppress/exempt fields.

Verification: cargo test (1524 passed, 2 ignored); cargo clippy clean on changed files (378 pre-existing warnings elsewhere, none new); sutra_review on the workspace runs end-to-end with the deviation engine intact and no spurious conventions parse error (rules.toml block removed). Cargo.toml was already modified in the working tree at session start; left untouched and unstaged.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (b7f6a4a vs de925f9) — verdict: needs-attention (1 medium, no critical/high).

Removals confirmed correctly scoped: ConventionsConfig, ConventionExemption, FcaEngine::check + tests, ConventionViolation (struct + re-export) all gone; check_inverse/ConventionMatch and detect_deviations untouched; deviation path still wired via src/tools/review.rs. The Option<toml::Value> catch-all + all_constraints ConstraintParseError correctly surfaces the removed block through the MCP tools (constraints list / orient / review include constraint_parse_errors).

[medium] rules.toml guard edit-path drops the removed-block parse error (src/bin/guard.rs:189-204 → src/guard.rs:850). The .sutra/rules.toml guard branch runs only check_proposed_rules_ratchet, which does `let (constraints, _errors) = parsed.all_constraints();` and discards errors. So editing rules.toml to add/keep a [conventions] block is accepted silently at edit time; the warning only appears later in review/list/orient. Verified against source.

Assessment (Claude): valid finding, but pre-existing — this branch has always been ratchet-only and dropped ALL parse errors (unknown kind, invalid glob included). This task added one more error type to a set the guard edit-path already ignored; it is not a regression from b7f6a4a. Filing as follow-up rather than reopening 289.
